run.question: List the top 5 largest Elasticsearch indices matching the pattern 'app-184-*' by document count. Show their names and doc counts.

report.summary: Read-only inventory question. The Elasticsearch listing of indices matching 'app-184-*' was requested sorted by docs.count descending; the first ten rows of that ordering were read back from the stored result. Five indices each report 500 documents and are the only rows at that level: app-184-ml-worker-2024.01.25, app-184-data-analytics-2024.01.10, app-184-engineering-api-2024.01.20, app-184-security-auth-2024.01.05 and app-184-platform-billing-2024.01.15 (all health green, status open). The very next row in the descending order (row 6, offset 5) already reports docs.count 1, so the remaining visible rows carry 1 document each. The ordering among the five 500-document indices is arbitrary (a tie), so no strict 1st-to-5th ranking is meaningful. The listing is a live catalog reading with no time range: the doc counts describe the moment of the query, not the incident window. No troubleshooting or change assessment was requested or performed, so no root cause is asserted.

claims.text: In the docs.count-descending listing of indices matching the pattern 'app-184-*', the five largest rows each report docs.count 500: app-184-ml-worker-2024.01.25 (500 docs, 47.8kb, green, open), app-184-data-analytics-2024.01.10 (500 docs, 46.9kb, green, open), app-184-engineering-api-2024.01.20 (500 docs, 31kb, green, open), app-184-security-auth-2024.01.05 (500 docs, 46.9kb, green, open) and app-184-platform-billing-2024.01.15 (500 docs, 30kb, green, open). These are offsets 0-4 of the sorted result.

The row immediately following the five 500-document indices in the same descending listing, app-184-ml-billing-2024.01.09, reports docs.count 1 (7.5kb, green, open); rows 6 through 10 of the listing (app-184-ml-billing-2024.01.09, app-184-data-db-2024.01.34, app-184-ml-billing-2024.01.08, app-184-data-db-2024.01.35, app-184-ml-billing-2024.01.07) all report docs.count 1, so no index at the 500 level appears after the fifth position.

Because all five top indices sit at exactly 500 documents, the ranking among them is a tie and their relative order in the returned list carries no meaning; a rank-by-size (store.size) ordering would differ, with app-184-ml-worker-2024.01.25 (47.8kb) and app-184-data-analytics-2024.01.10 / app-184-security-auth-2024.01.05 (46.9kb each) larger than app-184-engineering-api-2024.01.20 (31kb) and app-184-platform-billing-2024.01.15 (30kb). This ordering by size was read from the same rows, not independently verified by a size-sorted query.

gaps: Only the first 10 rows (offsets 0-9) of the docs.count-descending listing were read; the query's full match set was far larger than the display limit (the listing was refused as RESULT_TOO_LARGE and stored for slicing), so the doc counts of the indices outside those 10 rows are unknown rather than zero.

The listing carries no time filter: docs.count and store.size are catalog values as of the query instant and cannot show what these counts were at any earlier point inside the authorized window 2026-11-20T04:41:09Z to 2026-11-21T04:41:09Z.

An attempt to verify the number of indices with more than 1 document via a jq filter failed (JQ_RUNTIME_ERROR), and a second attempt returned one aggregate row too large to read (RESULT_TOO_LARGE with suggested_limit 0), so that count was not confirmed by aggregation; the conclusion rests on the sort order of the listing slice.
Whether any index named under the exact pattern 'app-184-*' was hidden by wildcard/expand_wildcards behavior (closed or hidden indices) was not checked beyond the default 'open' wildcard expansion.
next_steps: If a size-based ranking is needed, re-run elasticsearch_list_indices for pattern 'app-184-*' sorted by store.size:desc, since the top document counts are all tied at 500.

To confirm the document-count distribution across all matching indices, use an aggregation or a jq filter that emits only counts (for example a count of indices per docs.count bucket) instead of the whole listing.
